tagline: Market towns, covered bridges and a railroad's roundabout name.
intro: From Thurmont, at the foot of Catoctin Mountain, the loop heads east into Carroll County by Detour and Uniontown to Westminster, then back northwest through Taneytown to Emmitsburg, just below the Mason-Dixon line. Three covered bridges stand near Thurmont, at Loy's Station, Roddy Road and Utica Mills, and a lower loop wanders south by Union Bridge, Libertytown and New Windsor.
Union and Confederate soldiers both marched north on these roads to Gettysburg, and families and churches along them took in the wounded.

moments.title: Detour
moments.text: The village grew up along the Western Maryland Railway and, by tradition, takes its name from the roundabout way the railroad came to it.

moments.title: Taneytown
moments.text: George Washington found it but a small place, built up only along the street the road passes through, and mostly of wood.

moments.title: Emmitsburg
moments.text: Half the town burned on the night of June 23, 1863, set, folklore says, to keep supplies from the Confederates, and the battle came instead twelve miles north, at Gettysburg.
